title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of the 1976 de Rham notes. It is a typescript page, numbered '- 66 -' and headed 'IX', from Grothendieck's SGA 7 I, Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §5. It was apparently filed among the manuscript notes, perhaps reused as scrap paper: the faint pencil traces of the divided-power computations from the neighbouring pages show through.

Top half: end of the proof of a statement in §5.9.
- There is a homomorphism u_η : F_η → Y_η, where F is a group (Barsotti–Tate type) over a trait S with connected special fibre. Y_η is a Barsotti–Tate group (ℓ-divisible group) attached to the generic fibre, and Y_η^f is its 'fixed/finite' sub-part. The goal is to show that u_η factors through Y_η^f.
- Grothendieck composes to get v_η : F_η → Y_η/Y_η^f.
- By 5.6, the quotient extends to an ind-étale Barsotti–Tate group Z = M ⊗_Z (Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) over S.
- By Tate's theorem (homomorphisms of p-divisible groups over a DVR are determined by, and extend from, the generic fibre; cited in 5.8), v_η extends to v : F → Z.
- A homomorphism from a group with connected special fibre to an ind-étale group is zero. So v = 0, hence v_η = 0, and u_η lands in Y_η^f.

Bottom half: statement of Lemma 5.9.2, an extension principle for homomorphisms into a Néron-type group A over a trait.
- Data: an extension 1→G'→G→G''→1 with G'' smooth; a homomorphism u : G'→A; and v_η : G_η→A_η extending u_η.
- Conclusion: there is a unique v : G→A extending both v_η and u.
- Hypothesis: the pushout extension u_*G of G'' by A must be representable. This holds, for example, if G→G'' has a section locally for the finite locally free topology and A is quasi-projective (SGA 3 IV 6.3). A footnote says unpublished results of Raynaud show the condition always holds.
- The proof (on the following typescript page, not reproduced here) is the standard one. A homomorphism v extending u is the same as a group section of u_*G → G''. The generic section given by v_η extends by the Néron mapping property, since u_*G is a smooth A-torsor over the smooth G'', and the extension is automatically a homomorphism.
errors: 'Comme F est à fibre spéciale connexe … ce morphisme est nul' tacitly uses flatness of F (or Barsotti–Tate structure) so that vanishing on both fibres implies vanishing. This is standard and fine in context.
'savoir' is presumably the typescript's ellipsis for 'à savoir'.

ideas.what: Factorisation of u_η through the fixed part Y^f via extension to an ind-étale BT group and Tate's full faithfulness theorem, using connected special fibre ⇒ zero map to ind-étale
ideas.modern_name: Tate's theorem on p-divisible groups; connected–étale vanishing of homomorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (1967, p-divisible groups); Grothendieck in SGA 7 IX

ideas.what: Lemma 5.9.2: extension of homomorphisms G→A from the generic fibre plus a subgroup G', with A a Néron-type group, assuming the pushout extension is representable
ideas.modern_name: Néron mapping property applied to extensions/torsors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA 7 IX; cf. Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud, Néron Models
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exp. IX, Lemme 5.9.2, including the Raynaud footnote

ideas.what: Representability of pushout extensions of group schemes (Raynaud's then-unpublished results)
ideas.modern_name: Representability of quotients/torsors by group schemes over a DVR (Raynaud)
ideas.usually_credited_to: M. Raynaud (Faisceaux amples…, LNM 119, 1970, and related work)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX typescript, misfiled or reused as scrap among the 1976 divided-power de Rham notes. Its content, including the Raynaud footnote, is in print, so nothing on it is new. The only curiosity is archival: the juxtaposition is accidental.
transcription_corrections: Page identification: the typescript is SGA 7 I, Exp. IX, p. 66. It is not a manuscript page of cote 136. The pencil marks bleeding through are traces of the adjacent divided-power computations.

The faint inverted handwriting visible beneath the typescript (formulas such as φ_1(X_0^{(i)}), A_1, d ξ_i …) is show-through from the neighbouring manuscript pages and is not part of this page's content.
